json_data: An operating system (OS) is a collection of software that manages a computer’s hardware and applications by allocating resources.
An OS manages resources including memory, CPU, input/output devices, and file storage.
Users interact with an operating system through a user interface (UI), which can be either a graphical user interface (GUI) or a command-line interface (CLI).
All computer systems, from mainframes to mobile devices, require at least one operating system to perform tasks and run applications.
Microsoft Windows is the most widely used operating system worldwide, controlling 67% of the desktop, tablet, and console OS market.
Apple’s macOS ranks second in the desktop, tablet, and console OS market.
Android leads the mobile OS category with approximately 72.04% market share.
Apple’s iOS holds the second spot in the mobile OS category with 27.49% market share.
Linux is the most popular open source operating system, widely favored for its flexibility and security.
The history of the operating system began with early computers that required customized system software for task management.
Operating systems evolved to support multitasking and interactive interfaces, driven by advances in hardware and software.
The invention of the integrated circuit (IC) in the 1950s led to microchips, boosting processing power and reducing computer size.
In 1964, IBM introduced the OS/360, which standardized software across its mainframes and influenced future OS designs.
The OS/360 was the first multiprogramming operating system, capable of running numerous programs simultaneously on a single processor machine.
The OS/360 evolved into z/OS®, the modern OS for IBM mainframes.
The development of the time-sharing OS Unix in the 1960s and 1970s introduced concepts such as multitasking, portability, and a hierarchical file system.
Graphics processing units (GPUs) were introduced in the late 1980s and 1990s to handle graphics processing.
Today, GPUs are a standard feature in most computing systems, powering applications from gaming to machine learning.
Virtualization allows multiple virtual machines (VMs) to run on a single physical machine, with a hypervisor managing these VMs.
VMware is considered the leader in the virtualization and hypervisor market.
Containerization offers a more lightweight approach to running isolated applications compared to VMs, as containers do not include a full copy of the operating system.
An operating system manages and coordinates hardware and software, providing an environment where users can interact effectively.

Core functions of an OS include process management, memory management, file system management, device management, security and access control, networking, error detection and handling, resource allocation, and system performance monitoring.
The kernel is the central component of the OS, managing critical system processes and enabling interaction between software and hardware.
The process scheduler allocates CPU time to processes, ensuring efficient resource usage and managing multitasking.
The memory manager allocates and reallocates memory to processes, managing both RAM and virtual memory.
The Input/output (I/O) manager facilitates data communication between the system and external devices.
The file system manager organizes, retrieves, and secures files across various file systems.
An embedded operating system is designed to manage hardware resources in specialized devices and is optimized for resource-constrained environments.
A distributed operating system coordinates multiple independent computers to work together as a unified system, allowing resources from different machines to be shared.
A real-time operating system (RTOS) handles time-sensitive tasks with precise timing constraints, guaranteeing critical processes are completed within a specific time frame.
A network operating system (NOS) manages and coordinates the hardware and software resources of multiple computers connected in a network.
A cluster operating system manages a group of interconnected computers that work together as a single system, providing load balancing and fault tolerance.
Linux is an open source operating system widely used in desktops, servers, and embedded systems.
Microsoft Windows is one of the most widely used operating systems globally for personal and business use.
macOS is a Unix-like proprietary OS designed to run on Apple’s desktops, laptops, and workstations.
Apple iOS is a proprietary mobile operating system that runs on Apple mobile devices.
Android is an open source mobile operating system developed by Google, widely used in personal and business smartphone devices.
The AI operating systems market is projected to grow from USD 12.496 billion in 2024 to USD 29.297 billion by 2029.
AI-powered operating systems leverage machine learning and automation to predict user behaviors, optimize resource allocation, and adapt to changing workloads.
AI-driven security systems in leading operating systems like Windows and macOS identify and mitigate cyberthreats.
